raw_response:
Alright, let me think about this year. I got 24 mu and with just me and the old lady at home — the kids are off in town working — we gotta be careful how we spread ourselves. Last couple years I done 18 mu of wheat-maize and kept 6 mu in cotton, and that's about what we can handle. Same thing again this year.

The wheat's been in the ground since October. I laid down two bags of compound per mu before planting, and already went in with urea once when it greened up in March — about half a bag per mu. Winter was a bit dry, so I already watered once after the spring thaw. Still need to irrigate at jointing, which is right about now, and probably once more for grain filling. Electric pumping keeps getting more expensive but you can't skip water or the grain won't fill. Sprayed the herbicide in March for the weeds. If I see aphids come May I'll spray one time, otherwise I leave it alone. Looking at the stand, I figure I'll get about 450 jin per mu, same as usual — not a bumper year but decent.

Cotton I need to get planted in the next week or two, soon as the soil warms proper. I always buy fresh seed from the shop — Old Wang down the road uses the same kind and his cotton did alright last year. Cotton takes more looking after than grain, bollworms come mid-summer and you gotta spray two or three times. Picking in the fall is the killer — me and the wife can't do 6 mu by ourselves at our age, so I'll hire a couple of women from the village for a few days when it opens up. Cotton price has been soft but I keep some because you don't want everything tied up in grain.

Maize comes right after wheat harvest in June — no time to waste, you gotta turn the ground and get seed in within a week or the season's too short. Hybrid seed from the shop, same one everyone around here uses. Maize is easier than wheat if July rains come right. I usually do one big urea topdress when it's knee-high, about a bag per mu. Maybe one irrigation if it's dry. Should get around 500 jin per mu.

Money out is going to run around 11,000-12,000 yuan total for the year — seed, fertilizer, pesticide, water, and some hired hands for cotton picking. If the wheat and maize both come in decent, we clear enough to live on. One bad drought and it's tight. That's why I hold back some cash and why I don't go putting extra fertilizer on just because the shop tells me to.
